newsitem.title: USA: Most think Clinton won debate, polls show.
newsitem.headline: Most think Clinton won debate, polls show.

text.p: President Bill Clinton won Sunday night's presidential debate with Republican Bob Dole, according to three polls conducted immediately after the 90-minute encounter in Hartford, Connecticut.
A Gallup poll conducted for CNN found that 51 percent of Americans believed Clinton won the debate, compared to 32 percent who were more impressed with Dole's performance.
But seventy-four percent of the people polled said Dole did better than they expected.
A CBS News snap poll gave Clinton 50 percent to Dole's 28 percent, with 17 percent calling the debate a tie.
Results in an ABC News poll were similar, with 50 percent calling the debate a triumph for Clinton, compared to 29 percent for Dole. Nineteen percent said it was a tie.

The ABC poll showed that both candidates appeared to benefit modestly from their showing in the debate, with Clinton's support rising to 55 percent from 51 percent and Dole's backing inching to 41 percent from 40 percent.
Support for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, who was excluded from the debate, dipped to two percent from five percent in the ABC poll.

The latest Reuters daily tracking poll, conducted before the debate, showed Dole stranded 15 points behind Clinton, with 47.3 percent saying they would vote for the president, 31.9 percent for his Republican challenger, and 5.3 percent for independent Ross Perot.
The CNN poll had a margin of error of plus or minus four percentage points. The ABC poll had a margin of error of plus or minus 4.5 percentage points.
